messages.author: e89c8831c948bf5f
messages.subject: Geolocation, state-space model, data structure
parts:
Hello Stan

I'm working on a geolocation problem for fish at sea. The fish is tagged with sensors that measure environmental variables, in my case temperature and depth. 
I have implemented it in JAGS but convergent is very slow and I was wondering if stan would be a better option. 
One thing about translating the the problem is the lack of support for discrete parameters.

My hidden state (parameters) in the model is the location 
lon[t] and lat[t]

One of my response variable is temperature. To get the expected temperature at the location I use measurements from satellites at the location. So I have a 3D matrix SST with temperature measurements and the measurements from the tag y. So I use an index variable to extract the expected temperature.

lon_ind[t] <- trunc((lon[t] - min_lon + res) * res^-1)
lat_ind[t] <- trunc((lat[t] - min_lat + res) * res^-1)

mu[t] <- SST[lon_ind[t],lat_ind[t],t]
y[t] ~ dnorm(mu[t],tau_temp)

Is there any other method or data structure for the SST I could use to get the expected temperature that could by implemented in Stan?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Geolocation, state-space model, data structure
parts:
Hi Bob

This is part of my JAGS code which is not pretty. I also have another data source to estimate position (lon ,lat) which is not included in this model.

The thing is that lon_ind and lat_ind are the discrete parameters (Only a transformation of lon and lat). I was mainly wondering if anyone knew a better way to get the expected temperature (mu) from lon and lat without having to define the index variables (lon_ind and lat_ind).


data {  
    pi <- 3.141592653589
    res <- 0.25
    min_lon <- -50
    min_lat <- 50
    max_lon <- 10
    max_lat <- 70
    lon_start  <- -21.777
    lat_start <- 64.315
    tau_temp <- 4 #stdev 0.5 for temperature
}

model{    
    #First day
    lat_lim[1] <- size_lim[1]/111.2 #km to latitude
    #Keep within the box
    U_lat[1] <- min(max_lat, lat_start+lat_lim[1])
    L_lat[1] <- max(min_lat, lat_start-lat_lim[1])
    lat[1] ~ dunif(L_lat[1], U_lat[1])
    lon_lim[1] <- 360*sqrt( pow(size_lim[1],2)- pow((lat[1]-lat_start)*111.2,2)) / (2*pi*6371*cos(lat_start*pi/180))
    U_lon[1] <- min(max_lon, lon_start+lon_lim[1])
    L_lon[1] <- max(min_lon, lon_start-lon_lim[1])
    lon[1] ~ dunif(L_lon[1], U_lon[1])

    #In which grid-cell is salmon locted
    lon_ind[1] <- trunc((lon[1] - min_lon + res) * res^-1)
    lat_ind[1] <- trunc((lat[1] - min_lat + res) * res^-1)

    #Movement
    for (d in 2:N_d){
        #Movement
        #Change from km to degrees longitude
        lat_lim[d] <- size_lim[d]/111.2
        U_lat[d] <- min(max_lat, lat[d-1]+lat_lim[d])
    L_lat[d] <- max(min_lat, lat[d-1]-lat_lim[d])
#Move north-south
        lat[d] ~ dunif(L_lat[d], U_lat[d])# T(min_lat,max_lat) does not work
        #Movement limit for longitude dependent on latitudinal movement
        lon_lim[d] <- 360*sqrt( pow(size_lim[d],2)- pow((lat[d]-lat[d-1])*111.2,2)) / (2*pi*6371*cos(lat[d-1]*pi/180))
U_lon[d] <- min(max_lon, lon[d-1]+lon_lim[d])
    L_lon[d] <- max(min_lon, lon[d-1]-lon_lim[d])
lon[d] ~ dunif(L_lon[d], U_lon[d])
        #In which grid-cell is salmon locted
        lon_ind[d] <- trunc((lon[d] - min_lon + res) * res^-1)
        lat_ind[d] <- trunc((lat[d] - min_lat + res) * res^-1)
        #Land mask
        #O[d] ~ dbern(water[lon_ind[d],lat_ind[d]])
#Edit included in SST data did not work, check again
    }
    for (d in 1:N_d){
        #Expected temperature from position
        mu[d] <- SST[lon_ind[d],lat_ind[d],d]
        #Likelihood of temperature data
        temp[d] ~ dnorm(mu[d],tau_temp)

}
}
